patch_description: Revert to the higher-scoring 3-shell shared-CRZ backbone (nearest-neighbor, skip, antipodal rings, all keyed to theta_z, plus a shared theta_ry local layer) that previously achieved combined score 0.61, dropping the final-RY-mixer variant that regressed to 0.55. On top of that proven backbone, apply the targeted axis-mixing recommendation: in Shell 3 (the four antipodal, distance-4 pairs) swap CRZ for CRY while still reusing the same shared "theta_z" parameter name (so the parameter count stays at 2 distinct circuit parameters). Rationale: CRZ commutes with the RZ single-qubit layer and with the CRZ gates in shells 1/2, so all Z-generated rotations only ever dephase relative phases and never rotate Bloch vectors out of the Z-eigenbasis structure imposed by the local RZ layer -- this leaves a residual symmetry (global relative-phase invariance) that a state's Z-basis populations alone cannot break. Introducing a Y-axis controlled rotation only on the long-range antipodal links forces those particular qubit pairs to develop entanglement that is not diagonal in the same basis as the rest of the circuit, which should let the read-out observable pick up a genuinely different (non-commuting) correlation structure specifically from the hardest, most long-range-correlated validation examples, without adding any new trainable parameter.
